## Natural history notes

A tiny grass skipper characterized by its orange to golden-brown wings, narrow dark borders, slender body, and quick low flight just above vegetation. In Florida, it is found in wet grassy habitats such as marsh edges, wet prairies, pond margins, ditches, canals, and damp fields where sedges and grasses grow. Adults feed on nectar from small flowers and often perch low on grasses or sedges, while the caterpillars feed on grasses and sedges, using folded blades as shelters during development.
